minutes.headline: Board put the track and field engineering article on the special town meeting warrant and rejected the park design article.
minutes.summary: The board approved a liquor license for Kiku with a prorated fee, heard a report on selling or leasing the Brooks House, and held a joint session with the Stormwater Task Force on a utility fee versus the operating budget. It heard the superintendent on the failing track and field retaining wall, then finalized the special town meeting warrant. Track and field and the stormwater advisory were included, the accessibility/park design article failed, and the trust fund continuity bylaw failed.

what_happened.line: The Select Board voted unanimously to place the middle high school track and field engineering article on the special town meeting warrant.
The board voted 0-5 on the accessibility and park design article, which was moved so it could be voted down, and it did not go on the warrant.
The advisory article on stormwater funding mechanisms passed 4-1, and the trust fund continuity article failed 0-5.
The board approved the Kiku liquor license unanimously with the annual fee cut to one quarter for the rest of the calendar year.
In a joint session, the Stormwater Task Force and the board discussed a utility fee versus the operating budget; the track article was later moved to last on the warrant.

why_it_matters: Voters at the special town meeting will be asked to act on design and engineering for the track and field retaining wall, which could lead to a later construction request and tax impact.
The stormwater advisory article asks voters to weigh a dedicated utility fee against paying through the operating budget, which is funded mostly by taxes.
watch_next: October 27 Select Board meeting, where the board will make its recommendations on all special town meeting warrant articles.
The November 3 election, whose warrant the board approved, and the special town meeting warrant as finalized.
